newsitem.title: RUSSIA: OLYMPICS-DOPING CONTROL EXPERT LOSES IN EYE IN ASSAULT.
newsitem.headline: OLYMPICS-DOPING CONTROL EXPERT LOSES IN EYE IN ASSAULT.

text.p: A doping control expert at the Russian Olympic Committee lost an eye when he was severely beaten up in an attack his colleagues said could be linked to his anti-drugs work.

Yuri Vdovin has partial amnesia after the incident on a Moscow street in February. Collegues said Vdovin had doping samples with him when he was attacked. Random street violence is rare in the Russian capital.

Doping control workers complain a lack of cash has meant they no longer have access to Olympic Committee cars and must travel with samples by public transport, leaving them exposed to attacks from disgruntled or anxious sportsmen.

In the latest doping embarrassment for Moscow, cross-country skier Lyubov Yegorova was stripped of a gold medal this week after admitting taking the banned drug Bromantan before Sunday's five-km race at the world championships in Trondheim on Sunday.
